newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly end lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly end lower.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Monday in a moderate session, pressured by some some technical selling after an early rally on firmer cash prices stalled, industry sources said.
March slipped 1.5 cents to close at $2.167 per million British thermal units. April settled 1.5 cents higher at $2.107. Most other deferreds ended steady to down 3.9 cents.

"People are confused. Some people still think winter is going to hit and others think it's too late and spring is just around the corner," said one Texas-based trader, noting the complex rallied early today on slightly firmer cash prices.
While cool Texas temperatures today helped boost the cash, traders said forecasts for mostly seasonal weather in major market centers this week meant any rally could be a struggle.
But while most technical traders agreed March's close Friday below trendline support painted a bleak chart picture, some said the market was oversold and due for a bounce.

"I think we're closer to a bottom here. The market got very short in a short period of time and we haven't seen any correction," said another Texas trader, adding eastern storage, while well-above last year, was still basically flat with the three-year average.
Chartists pegged key support in March at the Nov 5 low at $2.12, with psychological support at $2. March resistance was seen in the low-$2.50s and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices edged up slightly Monday to near the $2.40 level. Midcon pipes were little changed in the $2.30-35 level. New York city gate gas was quoted steady to up slightly in the $2.90-95 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip eased 0.7 cent to $2.134. NYMEX said an estimated 30,793 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 34,195.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Monday.

On the KCBT, March finished four cents lower at $1.93, while deferreds ended steady to down two cents. The East/West spread widened by 2.5 cents to 23.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 263 lots traded, up from 143 on Friday.
